newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: Three World Court judges re-elected.
newsitem.headline: Three World Court judges re-elected.

text.p: Judges from the United States, Russia and Algeria were re-elected to the World Court on Wednesday, while eminent jurists from the Netherlands and Brazil were elected to a first term on the 15-member panel based at The Hague.
The voting took place concurrently in the 15-nation Security Council and the 185-member General Assembly, where absolute majorities were required for election.

Re-elected were Mohammed Bedjaoui of Algeria, the current President of the International Court of Justice, as the World Court is officially called; Stephen Schwebel of the United States; and Vladen Vereshchetin of Russia.

Also elected were Pieter Kooijmans, professor of public international law at the University of Leiden, who has represented the Netherlands on many U.N. and other legal bodies; and Jose Francisco Rezek, a justice of the Supreme Court of Brazil who was foreign minister from 1990 to 1992.
They will all serve nine-year terms on the court beginning on Feb. 6, 1997.
The World Court is the principal judicial arm of the United Nations, ruling on cases referred to it by governments and giving advisory opinions at the request of U.N. bodies.

The election was to fill vacancies resulting from the completion next February of the current terms of Bedjaoui, Schwebel and Vereshchetin, as well of judges Mohamed Shahabuddeen of Guyana and Luigi Ferrari Bravo of Italy.
There were 11 candidates for the five places, nominated by qualified legal groups in many countries.

Four of the candidates obtained the required absolute majority of votes in the 15-nation Security Council on the first round of balloting -- Bedjaoui (14), Kooijmans (8), Schwebel (15) and Vereshchetin (15). Rezek succeeded on the council's third ballot, with eight votes.

All five obtained the necessary majority in the General Assembly on the first round of balloting in that body, where Bedjaoui received 149 votes, Kooijmans 111, Rezek 97, Schwebel 110 and Vereshchetin 123.
